subject: v1.1 task 11.1 - provider inventory cache model, bounds, and limits (tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrInventoryCacheTests.cs) - attempt 2 re-review after the correction round
previous_review: docs/implementation/11.1/test-quality-review.json (attempt 1: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; TQ-11.1-1 HIGH, TQ-11.1-2/3 MEDIUM, TQ-11.1-4/5/6 LOW)
assessment: Every attempt-1 finding is genuinely closed by a test that fails when the corresponding production behavior is broken. Independent mutation testing in a throwaway copy (/tmp/final-review/test-quality/mut) reproduced each sensitivity claim: the FromLimits binding test fails on both a wrong time unit and swapped record/byte fields; the cache-boundary provider-failure test fails when TryStore extends the window on lastError and when the eviction boundary is loosened from >= to >; the credential-bearing member-type denylist fails when an ArrConnection member is added to a cache type; the byte boundary pair fails when the comparison is made inclusive; the retained-set assertion fails when a rejected over-bound store displaces the retained set; and the distinctness test fails when a MetadataStateEntry member is added to ArrInventoryCacheEntry. No hidden skips, deterministic fixed-time tests, and all tests exercise real production types with no doubles. One new LOW test-quality item remains: the credential-bearing denylist is direct-member-only and does not recurse into the canonical nested types (MatchCandidate/BadgeMetadata/ArrRecordIdentity), so its own comment overstates that it checks the cache object graph; no transitive credential-bearing member exists today. Two INFORMATIONAL observations only. Counts independently reproduced: focused 24 passed / 0 skipped / 24 total; default 1387 passed / 63 skipped / 1450 total.

findings.description: InventoryCacheTypesExposeNoCredentialBearingMembers is a direct-member denylist only: EnumerateMemberTypes unwraps the member types of the four cache model types one level (plus generics/arrays) but does not recurse into the members of those member types. The test comment claims it 'checks the member types of the cache object graph' and 'fails if ... a secret lease ... is added to any cache type', yet a credential-bearing member added to a canonical nested type that the cache retains by reference (MatchCandidate, BadgeMetadata, ArrRecordIdentity, ArrProvider, or ArrProviderError) would not be detected, and the name heuristic does not inspect those types at all. Today no transitive credential-bearing member exists, so this is a future-regression gap, not a present false confidence in shipped behavior.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrInventoryCacheTests.cs:141-171 (direct-member enumeration), 432-473 (EnumerateMemberTypes/Unwrap do not recurse into member types' own members).
tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrInventoryCacheTests.cs:475-481 (IsSecretName is applied only to the three named cache types, not to nested canonical types).
src/ArrTags/Matching/MatchCandidate.cs:98-148 and src/ArrTags/Metadata/BadgeMetadata.cs:122-212 expose only canonical, non-credential member types today.
findings.recommended_action: Either make the credential-bearing type guard recursive over the retained object graph (with a visited set and cycle guard), or reword the test comment to state explicitly that it inspects direct members of the four cache model types and does not traverse nested canonical types.

findings.description: LastErrorSatisfiesTheBoundedRedactedProviderErrorContract asserts truncation against ArrProviderError.MaxMessageLength rather than pinning the numeric bound (512). The test therefore verifies that truncation happens and that the property surface is exactly Code/Message/Retryability, but a future reduction of MaxMessageLength would not fail it. ADR-020 clause 4 states the contract as 'bounded and redacted' without fixing 512, so no documented requirement is violated.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArrInventoryCacheTests.cs:187-195.
docs/decisions.md ADR-020 clause 4 (bounded/redacted contract, no numeric bound).
findings.recommended_action: None required; optionally pin 512 if the value becomes a fixed ADR-020 contract.

findings.description: The cache-boundary failure test demonstrates non-extension of the window when a failure is stored at the original ObservedAt, but the cache has no failure-only write that retains a previously stored set; TryStore always replaces from the caller-supplied observedAt and records. The 'provider failure keeps the last-known-good set' guarantee is therefore established as 'the failure annotation does not alter the computed window', and the retention path itself is owned by task 11.2 when a caller exists. The worker report and the ArrInventoryCache/ArrInventoryCacheEntry remarks document this scoping honestly, so it is not a false claim.
